title: Pagila DVD rental
summary: Four wide tables built from the 22 raw pagila tables, published to the Library, with the business's shared vocabulary defined on top of them.
decisions: Payments are kept as their own table (one per till receipt) and also rolled up onto each rental as amount_paid; revenue questions use payments, rental-behaviour questions use rentals.
A rental is late when it came back after the film's rental_duration; still-out rentals have is_late = null so they don't count either way.
Films' special_features (a text array) became four boolean columns instead of a text blob.
Customer email is kept (sample data); street address and phone are dropped, city/district/country stay.
Raw pagila tables stay visible; only the four clean tables are published to the Library.

definitions.measures: measures/*.json — one aggregation per table, no baked-in filters
definitions.segments: segments/*.json — late returns, still out, active customers, frequent renters (>= 30 rentals), family friendly, never rented
definitions.metrics: metrics/*.json — Revenue, Rentals, Active renters, Late return rate, Average days out; monthly default; saved in Library / Metrics

checks: build.sh runs every card after creation and fails on an error or an empty result; row counts above were reconciled against the raw tables before the transforms were committed.
